11._section_summary: This section, titled 'Inter-scale correlations', describes an initial examination of correlates of acceptance of cosmetic surgery in Brazil. It reports bivariate correlations between the ACSS score, General body appreciation, actual-ideal body weight discrepancy, SATAQ-3 subscales, participant age, and self-reported BMI for women and men separately. The findings indicate significant correlations between higher ACSS scores and lower General body appreciation, greater body weight discrepancy, higher SATAQ-3 scores, and higher self-reported BMI for both genders, with a minor exception for men.

6._section_summary: This section, titled 'Inter-scale correlations', describes an initial examination of correlates of acceptance of cosmetic surgery in Brazil. It reports bivariate correlations between the ACSS score, General body appreciation, actual-ideal body weight discrepancy, SATAQ-3 subscales, participant age, and self-reported BMI for women and men separately. 7.evidence_source: Specifically, we found that higher acceptance of cosmetic surgery was significantly correlated with lower General body appreciation, greater internalisation of media messages about appearance (all four SATAQ-3 subscales among women, and three of the four subscales among men), and a higher self-reported BMI.
7._section_summary: This discussion section details the findings of the present study, focusing on the psychometric properties of the Portuguese ACSS and BAS among Brazilian adults. It confirms a three-factor structure for the ACSS and a two-factor structure for the BAS, discusses convergent validity, and notes few significant sex differences in cosmetic surgery acceptance. The section also addresses study limitations, including sample size disparities and lack of socioeconomic data.
